Shri Brijendra Kumar Vaishya - Advocate for the peti  Shri Y. Shukla - PL for the respondents/ State.
 Shri Alok Hoonka and Shri Amit Dubey - Advocate for   no. 4.
 ORDER

The petitioner has filed this petition seeking the following reliefs :-
I. Direct the respondents to pay the compensation asper current market rate and allot the land in lieu to land.
II. Quash the impugned order dated 26.07.2013passed by Sub-Divisional Officer/Land Acquisition Officer Singrauli (Annexure-P/7).
IIIl. Any other relief or writ or direction or order, which this Hon'ble Court deems fit and proper, looking to the facts and circumstances of the case be kindly awarded to the petitioner including the cost of petition"
2.

Briefly stated facts of the case are that the petitioner is owner of land khasra No.
1176/2ka, area 0.29 hectare situated at village Harrahwa Tahsil and District Singrauli (M.P.).
The land in question is recorded in the name of the petitioner.

One Sthal Panchnama was prepared in presence of the representative of the Reliance Sashan Rambali Singh vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 5 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/158558341/

sentences.text: In the Sthal Panchnama, pakka houses and hand pump were found.
On 04.07.2013 respondent No.2 issued a notice to the petitioner under section 9 (1) of the Land Acquisition Act for acquisition of the Land total area 0.29 hectare.
The petitioner has filed an objection in respect of adequate compensation before the Land Acquisition Officer Singrauli as well as Collector Singrauli.
On 20.11.2013 petitioner filed an application before the Collector Singrauli for just and proper compensation.
Respondent No. 4 raised one objectionbefore the Land Acquisition Officer Singrauli.
On the objection of the respondent No.4 Tahsildar, Tahsil Singrauli held one inquiry.

3. It is pointed out that the representation (Annexure P/4) dated 20.11.2013 has already been filed by the petitioner and is pending consideration before respondent No.2 and has not been decided till date.
An innocuous prayer is made to direct the respondent No.2 to consider and decide the representation submitted by the petitioner.
4. Counsel appearing for the respondents/ State as well as the counsel appearing for the respondent no. 4 have no objection to the limited prayer made by the counsel for the petitioner.

5. In such circumstances, this petition is disposed off by directing the petitioner to file a certified copy of this order to the respondent No.2 who, in turn, is directed to take a final decision on the representation dated 20.11.2013 of the petitioner (if not already decided) within a period of 90 days from the date of receipt of certified copy of this order, after giving an opportunity of hearing to all the effected parties.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-JBP:17925 3 WP-20972-2013 6.
Needless to mention that this Court has not expressed any opinion on the merits of the case.
7. Accordingly, the petition is disposed of finally in above terms.
